title: Gujarat HC Issues Notice Over Mass Voter Deletions
excerpt: Court seeks answers on thousands of alleged fake Form 7 objections that erased nearly 74 lakh names from electoral rolls.
body:
Gujarat's High Court stepped squarely into one of India's most consequential electoral disputes on Friday, issuing notice on petitions that demand a Special Investigation Team probe into alleged mass voter deletions during the state's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

**What the court did:**
Justice Hemant Prachchhak issued notice on petitions alleging thousands of fake Form 7 objections during the SIR, with petitioners seeking an SIT probe into the deletions and alleged lapses by election authorities — posting the matter for further hearing on July 7.

**The scale of the deletions:**
Two senior Congress leaders from Surat — Vipulkumar Udhnawala, the district Congress president, and Vinod Patil, chief organiser of the Seva Dal — filed the special civil application on February 10, challenging the SIR and alleging widespread irregularities and arbitrary deletions. The Election Commission ran the SIR from November 4, 2025 to December 14, and the draft rolls published on December 19 showed a drop of nearly 74 lakh voters — from 5.08 crore to 4.34 crore electors across Gujarat. The controversy centres on the bulk filing of Form 7 applications, with opposition parties accusing organised actors of misusing the statutory objection form to systematically delete eligible voters.

**The legal argument:**
Petitioners claim that defective objections were entertained and acted upon without serving notice or granting affected voters a chance to be heard — a direct violation of principles of natural justice and Rule 21A. The plea also invokes a Supreme Court precedent in *Lal Babu Hussein v. Electoral Registration Officer*, which holds that once a name appears on the draft roll, the burden of proof lies on the objector — a principle petitioners say election authorities ignored.

**What to watch:**
With the next hearing set for July 7, the court's decision on whether to order an SIT probe or compel the Election Commission to restore deleted names will signal how seriously India's judiciary guards the right to vote.
